note: THE LOOP FAILS AS MOTION even though every frame is fine. f15, f18, f21 (u=0.313/0.375/0.438) are nearly identical: the animal hangs just under the lid for a full second. Cause: beat 1 peels off with 34*t^2, which moves ~9px by mid-beat. A quarter of the cycle is dead air, and a body that hangs is not a body that cannot stop. This is exactly the difference the MOTION-BRIEF warns about - a frame that reads well and a loop that reads well are not the same achievement.

note: Read the full-res frame f-0033 (u=0.688, deep in the fall) and it was a solid black clot. Cause: with the wings squeezed to openX~0.28, four wing planes plus sixteen veins plus both contours land inside a 60px strip. Fixed with the ink ladder rather than opacity (there is none in this world): a closing wing steps its fill 2 -> 1 -> 0 and drops from 4 veins to 2 to 1, on the grounds that a closed wing shows its pale underside. Three discrete levels, no interpolation, and the steps fall inside the fastest part of the fall so they do not pop.
